results.question: According to Raghavendra Vijaya, whose exposition of the Brahma Sutras is praised in verse 8, and what does the verse say happens to a scholar who hears it?
results.answer: The verse praises the exposition of the Brahma Sutras by Sri Vyasaraja [source: kavya_alankara/raghavendra_vijaya/sarga_1::8 | mula_sa]. It says that any scholar, even one who is proud, will become his devoted disciple upon hearing it [source: kavya_alankara/raghavendra_vijaya/sarga_1::8 | translation_en_human].

results.question: Compare what Prahlada Nrsimha Stotra verse 1 itself says with what its Satyadharmiya commentary explains about the phrase 'brahmadayah suraganah' (Brahma and the gods).
results.answer:
Verse 1 states: "श्रीप्रह्राद उवाच | ब्रह्मादयः सुरगणाः मुनयोऽथ सिद्धाः सत्वैकतानमतयो वचसां प्रवाहैः ।" [stotra/PrahladaKrutaNarasimha::1 | mula_sa | lang=sa]

The Satyadharmiya commentary explains that "ब्रह्मादयः सुरगणा" refers to Brahma, the gods, and sages, and that "सत्त्वैकतानमतयः" means those whose minds are fixed on the single truth of the Self. [stotra/PrahladaKrutaNarasimha::1 | commentary_sa__satyadharmiya | lang=sa]

results.question: Using the Mahabharata Kannada Bhishma Parva passages, describe both how Yudhishthira fed and camped his army, and how he identified his own soldiers on the battlefield.
results.answer: Yudhishthira ordered the best food and fodder for all his soldiers and their vehicles [source: itihasa/mahabharata_kannada/bhishma_parva::0601001-12].  He also had thousands of camps set up around the Samanta Panchaka [source: itihasa/mahabharata_kannada/bhishma_parva::0601001-8].  Yudhishthira gave his soldiers insignia, signs, and ornaments [source: itihasa/mahabharata_kannada/bhishma_parva::0601001-14].

results.question: In Raghavendra Vijaya verse 5, what is being compared to a diamond, and why?
results.answer:
In Raghavendra Vijaya verse 5, the points of view of Trivikramapanditacharya in his literary masterpieces are being compared to a diamond. [source: kavya_alankara/raghavendra_vijaya/sarga_1::5] 

They are being compared to a diamond because, just as a diamond, though very hard, is admired by experts when set in fine gold, so too the composition of Trivikrama Pandita, though challenging and dense, is praised by wise poets when appreciated for its brilliant phrasing and meter. [source: kavya_alankara/raghavendra_vijaya/sarga_1::5]

results.answer: The Prahlada Nrsimha Stotra states that true devotion to the divine, as exemplified by the twelve virtues (knowledge, truthfulness, self-control, tranquility, absence of envy, humility, forbearance, non-greed, and generosity), is more effective than material qualifications. results.question: What does Raghavendra Vijaya verse 1 ask Narasimha's claw to grant, and to whom?
results.answer:
[kavya_alankara/raghavendra_vijaya/sarga_1::1 | translation_en_human]
Let the claws of Lord Sri Narasimha who has taken ten different incarnations for the purpose of bestowing the deserving men and women who are devoted to Him with the four objects of a soul viz Dharma - Artha - Kama - Moksha bless me with prosperity. 
[kavya_alankara/raghavendra_vijaya/sarga_1::1 | translation_en_ai]
May the claw of the glorious Lord Lakshmi-Narasimha, who assumes ten divine incarnations to bestow all desired blessings upon His devotees, grant me spiritual and material prosperity.
